title: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.40636v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: An observer sees only part of the surrounding world, yet must keep track of what lies beyond the current view. Spatial perception therefore involves more than recognizing individual images: it calls for a persistent spatial state that is updated under self-motion and used to guide action. Do visual foundation models provide representations that support such a state? We study this question through four levels of spatial capability---spatial structure, object persistence, predictive spatial update, and actionability---using frozen-feature probes on ten representations under streaming egocentric observations of static indoor environments. The resulting capability profiles vary across tasks, network layers, and prefix lengths: strong readout of the visible scene does not ensure accurate object persistence or future-feature retrieval. translated_title: 视觉基础模型中空间状态表征的探测
translated_abstract: 观察者只能看到周围世界的一部分，却必须追踪当前视野之外的事物。因此，空间感知不仅仅是识别单个图像：它需要一个持久的空间状态，该状态在自身运动过程中被更新，并用于指导行动。视觉基础模型是否提供了支持这种状态的表征？我们通过四个层次的空间能力来研究这个问题——空间结构、物体持续性、预测性空间更新和可行动性——在静态室内环境的流式自我中心观测下，对十种表征使用冻结特征探针进行研究。所得到的能力特征因任务、网络层和前缀长度而异：对可见场景的强大读取能力并不能保证准确的物体持续性或未来特征检索。匹配的对照实验将读取准确性与对视觉历史和运动的依赖区分开来。（原文摘要末尾截断）
tldr: 该论文通过四个层次的空间能力（空间结构、物体持续性、预测性空间更新和可行动性）探测十种视觉基础模型的表征，发现模型对可见场景的强大读取能力并不能保证物体持续性和未来空间预测能力。
en_tdlr: This paper probes ten visual foundation model representations across four levels of spatial capability—spatial structure, object persistence, predictive spatial update, and actionability—revealing that strong readout of the visible scene does not ensure accurate object persistence or future-feature retrieval.
